strategyOwner: Allison Morgan / GTMx outbound (Tim Shaw thread)
headline: Your GrowFlow waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing licensed cannabis operators into the right GrowFlow Retail, Wholesale, Marketplace, or compliance offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Tim Shaw, CEO.
productSummary: GrowFlow (growflow.com) is a cannabis seed-to-consumer SaaS platform: Retail POS + inventory + compliance for dispensaries; Wholesale for cultivators, processors, manufacturers, and distributors; Live Marketplace linking wholesaler inventory to retailer ordering; and eCommerce tied to live Retail stock. Verified integrations with Metrc, BioTrack, and Washington CCRS, plus Weedmaps, Leafly, SpringBig, and an open API. Built for single stores through multi-state operators. Site claim: preferred cannabis compliance and dispensary software for thousands of licensed US operators. Public retail footprint pages list AK, CA, CO, MI, MT, NY, OK, OR, SD, WA. Tim Shaw is CEO (tim@growflow.com).
coreInsight: Tim sells one GrowFlow seed-to-consumer platform, not a different product per state. State and license type (retail vs wholesale) are merge tags after routing, not a second waterfall. The single routing signal is competitor_pos: which cannabis POS or seed-to-sale stack a lead source can already see (Dutchie/Greenbits/LeafLogix, other retail POS, adjacent marketplace/menu-only tools, or none). That ladder maps to GrowFlow's live offers — competitor switch + migration, side-by-side compliance/ops comparison, Marketplace + Wholesale consolidation, then a soft compliance hours-saved playbook for the rest of the licensed TAM.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is which cannabis POS they already run
sections.takeaway: Cannabis directories, job posts, menu/partner badges, and public stack mentions already show Dutchie, Flowhub, Treez, Meadow, Blaze, Cova, or adjacent marketplace tools. That competitor_pos is stronger than a title guess and cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every licensed operator in GrowFlow states
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Dutchie-family POS first, then other retail POS, then adjacent marketplace/menu-only stacks, then every remaining licensed operator in GrowFlow's footprint.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each competitor_pos band gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Dutchie gets a Switch + Migration Brief. Other POS gets a Compliance vs Ops Comparison. Adjacent stacks get a Marketplace + Wholesale Brief. The rest get the GrowFlow Compliance Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the POS, win the comparison, consolidate wholesale, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always licensed cannabis operators in GrowFlow states. State and license type are merge tags. A/Bs sit on exclusive routes (compliance support vs operational efficiency — matching Allison's P.S.).

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the stack already visible on their storefront
sections.takeaway: Notice the POS or adjacent tool, poke the compliance/ops/hours gap that stack implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the Dutchie-switch route first
sections.takeaway: Start where competitor_pos already shows Dutchie/Greenbits/LeafLogix. Prove reply density, then roll other-POS, Marketplace/Wholesale, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: State cannabis license directories + Weedmaps/Leafly storefronts are the TAM GrowFlow already sells into: licensed retail and wholesale operators in AK, CA, CO, MI, MT, NY, OK, OR, SD, WA (and adjacent markets GrowFlow can serve). Exact public TAM account count is not published on growflow.com; treat size as estimated (see growflow-magnet-flags.txt) and keep each launch tier >=~1,500 contacts where possible.

The same scrape/enrichment pass returns competitor_pos: Dutchie (incl. Greenbits/LeafLogix), other retail POS (Flowhub, Treez, Meadow, Blaze, Cova), adjacent marketplace/menu tools (Leaflink/Nabis/Weedmaps-menu-only), or none — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live GrowFlow positioning (Retail POS + Metrc/BioTrack/CCRS compliance, Wholesale seed-to-sale, Live Marketplace, eCommerce) plus public proof language (thousands of licensed operators; named testimonials on growflow.com).
State, license_type (retail vs wholesale), and buyer title (Owner / Ops / Compliance) are scrape filters and merge tags, not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the account is routed.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_pos_family = dutchie (Dutchie, Greenbits, LeafLogix / Dutchie POS) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They already pay for the market-leading retail ecosystem. Strongest switch intent for GrowFlow Retail + compliance (Metrc/BioTrack/CCRS) with a migration magnet.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_pos_family = other_retail_pos (Flowhub, Treez, Meadow, Blaze, Cova, BioTrackTHC retail, MJ Freeway/Akerna legacy) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They run a competing retail POS. Side-by-side GrowFlow pitch on effortless compliance, inventory, and hours saved — matching Allison's compliance vs efficiency A/B.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_pos_family = adjacent_stack (Leaflink-only, Nabis-only, Weedmaps/Leafly menu-only, SpringBig-only, Bleaum-only, no full POS brand) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They have ordering/menu/loyalty tools without a unified seed-to-sale POS. Maps to GrowFlow Live Marketplace + Wholesale/Retail consolidation.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (licensed operators in GrowFlow states). Softest CTA around compliance automation, hours back, and seed-to-consumer clarity. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Dutchie-family POS detected
tiers.trigger: competitor_pos shows Dutchie, Greenbits, or LeafLogix / Dutchie POS; licensed operator in GrowFlow footprint; not already a GrowFlow customer
tiers.pain: They are already funding the dominant cannabis retail stack and still burning hours on track-and-trace reconciliations, inventory intake, and multi-store reporting.
tiers.valueProp: Dutchie Switch + Migration Brief: GrowFlow Retail with Metrc/BioTrack/CCRS-native compliance and a free-migration path off Dutchie lock-in.
tiers.dataSource: Weedmaps/Leafly + license directories + BuiltWith/job POS mentions

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Other retail POS detected
tiers.trigger: competitor_pos shows Flowhub, Treez, Meadow, Blaze, Cova, BioTrackTHC retail, or MJ Freeway/Akerna legacy; not Tier 1; not already_customer
tiers.pain: Competing POS still forces jumping between inventory, budtender UX, and state reporting — compliance risk and hours leak.
tiers.valueProp: Compliance vs Ops Comparison: GrowFlow Retail/Wholesale vs their POS on automated reporting, package-level inventory, and hours saved.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Adjacent marketplace/menu stack
tiers.trigger: competitor_pos_family=adjacent_stack (Leaflink/Nabis/Weedmaps-menu/SpringBig/Bleaum only); no Tier 1-2; not already_customer
tiers.pain: Ordering and menus live outside a unified seed-to-sale POS — stale stock sheets and email ping-pong with wholesalers.
tiers.valueProp: Marketplace + Wholesale Brief: GrowFlow Live Marketplace + Wholesale for live inventory, labs, manifests, invoices.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining licensed operators in GrowFlow states
tiers.trigger: in_tam licensed cannabis operator (retail or wholesale) in GrowFlow footprint with buyer Owner/GM/Ops/Compliance and no Tier 1-3 competitor_pos match
tiers.pain: Most licensed operators know compliance reporting and inventory are painful but have not publicly exposed a POS brand — so hours burn on spreadsheets and state reconciliations.
tiers.valueProp: Soft GrowFlow Compliance Playbook: practical paths into Retail, Wholesale, Marketplace, and Metrc/BioTrack/CCRS automation — soft CTA, site proof of thousands of licensed operators.
tiers.dataSource: State license directories after in_tam gate
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM
